list: 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze; 28 hidden on PlayStation; no online trophies
list_source: Names, descriptions and grades as published on PlayStation and tracked by Exophase and PSNProfiles (lists frozen 18 Nov 2026; the two agree on every name, description and grade). Rockstar, Sony and Microsoft have not published a separate official list; where a count comes from a tracker it is marked as such. No Rockstar logo or artwork is used anywhere in this guide.

sources.exophase: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list (names, descriptions, grades)
sources.gamemapa: GameMapa — All 55 GTA 6 Trophies (counts: 397 stunts, 18 card sets, 80 challenges, 500-profile actions)
sources.gamesradar: GamesRadar+ — GTA 6 trophy list (full list cross-checked against PowerPyx)
sources.gtascoop: GTA Scoop — GTA 6 Trophies & Achievements (only possibly missable trophy; no mission replay; cheats disable trophies)
sources.mobalytics: Mobalytics — GTA 6 Full Trophy List & Walkthrough (one possible missable trophy; free roam after the story)
sources.powerpyx: PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide & roadmap (platinum ~200 hours, one playthrough, no DLC/multiplayer needed)
sources.psnprofiles: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (names, descriptions, grades, PSN progress counts)
sources.pushsquare: Push Square — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Roadmap (100% checklist appears after the story; free roam continues after the finale)
sources.thegamershub: The Gamers Hub — GTA 6 Trophy List (100% checklist has 35 requirements)

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. PowerPyx puts the whole run at about 200 hours in a single playthrough, with no multiplayer and no DLC needed, and Push Square notes the 100% completion checklist only appears after the story, so plan on story first, then cleanup in free roam. Tick trophies off in this tracker as you go; the progress bar at the top is your countdown to this one.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and it unlocks as part of the story. This is Jason's first mission, so it should be one of the first trophies you ever earn. There is no mission replay in GTA VI (per GTA Scoop), but story trophies unlock automatically when you complete their mission, so you cannot skip past this one.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete Chapter 1 and it unlocks automatically. Before you leave Chapter 1, meditate at the spot at Jason's house — PowerPyx and GTABase flag that spot as the one meditation location that may not be reachable later, and it is the only thing in the whole list reported as possibly missable (see Positive Mental Attitude). Otherwise just play the chapter through.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete Chapter 2 and it unlocks automatically. Keep the name as PlayStation publishes it — with the asterisks — when you search for it on your console. Nothing special to do here; the chapter's missions carry you to it.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete Chapter 3 and it unlocks automatically. By this point the map is opening up; use the gaps between missions to try activities and start the side strands, since several trophies (Master of None, the stranger missions) are easiest while you are already out in the world.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete Chapter 4 and it unlocks automatically. One chapter remains after this one, so if you have been putting off the side content, the lull before the finale is a good time to clear stranger strands and activities before the story ends.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable, and the gold for finishing the game: complete the final mission. Push Square confirms that after the finale you can keep exploring Leonida in free roam for as long as you like, and the 100% completion checklist appears at that point — so the finale is the start of the cleanup phase, not the end of the trophy hunt. Do not turn cheats on: multiple guides report cheats disable trophies and saving.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies unlock automatically on completion, so play the mission through — there is no separate objective to chase and no way to miss it.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission The Cartel Heist. It unlocks automatically when the mission ends. Heist missions are story beats, not the repeatable robberies that the crime trophies (Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play) ask for.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission Child's Play. Like every mission trophy in this list it unlocks on completion, so just play the mission to its end.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission Headliners. The name is stylised as PlayStation publishes it (DWNFALL). No extra objective — finish the mission and the trophy follows.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the Vice City airport, and the same location matters for the Catch Me If You Can trophy later — but this one is just the mission, finished, and it unlocks on its own.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Story trophy, unmissable: complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. The last of the named-mission story trophies; after this, the remaining story trophies are the chapter completions and the finale. Finish the mission and it unlocks automatically.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: The gold for finishing everything: attain 100% completion. The checklist appears under Progress > Stats after the story (Push Square), and The Gamers Hub counts 35 requirements on it. It is the hardest single trophy — PowerPyx's ~200-hour platinum estimate is mostly this checklist — and it sweeps up the collectibles, activities and exploration trophies, so chase it last and let it pull the rest along. Check the in-game checklist often; it is the authoritative list of what is left.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete any 250 stunts — jumps, under-bridge flights, Knife Flights and base jumps all count (GameMapa). There are 397 stunts in total, so you only need about two-thirds of them; pick the easy ones first and use the stunt checklist in the game to avoid repeating ones you have done. Stunts are the silver that takes the longest after the shooting range, so start early and grab them whenever you pass one.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once: fishing, hunting, golf, the shooting range, pool, basketball, a video game, a race and a stunt (GameMapa). You do not need to be good at any of them — one attempt at each is enough. This is a good early trophy: while you are working through the other activity trophies, tick each type off once and it will pop on its own.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges (the count PlayStation tracks). This is the most skill-gated silver: learn each challenge's scoring, practise the weapon types you are weakest with, and use the range's own retry loop — attempts are unlimited, so a bad run costs nothing but time. Gold every challenge and the trophy pops; do it in chunks between story missions rather than in one sitting.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone races are a repeatable activity, so losing a race costs nothing — retry the location until you win it, then move to the next. Keep a note of which locations you have won at; the tracker in this guide is a good place for it, since the game does not always make it obvious which ones are done.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Work through the race types across Leonida (street, off-road and the rest) and vary the events; each first win counts. Pair this with Master of None, since a race attempt is one of its 9 activity types.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so you will meet the mechanics anyway; the challenge against Cal is the competitive version of it. Learn the fishing timing first on free fishing, then take the challenge — and retry as needed, since fishing challenges are repeatable.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish a full game at an arcade machine, not just start one. Arcades are scattered around Leonida; pick a game you can finish quickly and play it through. This also counts as one of the 9 activity types for Master of None.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Side-mission trophy: complete the final mission for Andy — GTA Scoop names that last mission Puff Puff Pass. Andy is one of five named contacts with their own mission chains (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), each ending in a trophy. Work through Andy's missions as they appear and the trophy unlocks when his strand ends.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Side-mission trophy: complete the final mission for Kenton. Kenton's strand is one of five named contact chains, each ending in its own trophy. Follow his missions as they unlock and the trophy pops when his last one is done — nothing extra is needed beyond finishing the strand.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Side-mission trophy: complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's chain is one of the five named contact strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone). Play his missions through to the end of the strand and the trophy unlocks with the last one.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida — the Strangers & Freaks style encounters, marked on the map as you explore. This is the silver for the stranger content: find the strangers, play each strand to its end, and count to eight. It pairs naturally with The Goodtime State (explore all of Leonida), since finding strangers means covering the map.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Side-mission trophy: complete the final mission for Randy. Randy's strand is one of the five named contact chains. Work through his missions as they appear; the trophy unlocks when his final mission is complete.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Side-mission trophy: complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone's strand is the last of the five named contact chains (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone). Finish his final mission and the trophy pops — and with the other four contact trophies, the side-mission set is done.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — and this is the ONE trophy in the list reported as possibly missable, so read this carefully. PowerPyx and GTABase (via GTA Scoop and GameMapa) flag that one meditation spot sits at Jason's house in Chapter 1 and may not be reachable later, so meditate there before you finish Chapter 1. The other 17 spots can be visited any time in free roam. If you are past Chapter 1 and never meditated at Jason's house, check whether the spot is still open before assuming the trophy is lost — reports call it 'possibly' missable, not confirmed.
trophies.missable_note: One meditation spot at Jason's house may only be reachable in Chapter 1 (PowerPyx/GTABase). Meditate there before finishing Chapter 1.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Hunting is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so the mechanics will already be familiar; this trophy asks for a specific, unique animal tied to Bret's request rather than any hunt. Follow Bret's strand to learn which animal and where it roams, then track and take it down.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — there are 18 sets in total (GameMapa), so you only need three of them. Cards are found across Leonida; pick the sets you are closest to finishing and hunt their missing cards first. This is a pure collectible grind, so it fits the cleanup phase after the story, when you can roam freely.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app to scan 100 locations — landmarks, curiosities and sculptures (GameMapa). WAiNK It is the in-game scanning app: point it at a point of interest and log it. A hundred sounds like a lot, but Leonida is full of scannable spots, and this pairs perfectly with The Goodtime State (explore all 52 areas) and Whip It Good (discover 100 vehicles — a WAiNK scan is enough for a vehicle, per GameMapa). Scan everything you pass and the count climbs on its own.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the 80 challenges (GameMapa). Challenges are the game's assorted side goals — the 100% checklist tracks them — so work through the ones that suit your playstyle first and let the count build across the whole run. You only need 50 of 80, so skip any challenge that fights you and come back to it later, if at all.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up to a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. Do it in a fast car with an escape route in mind — open roads out of the city beat tight streets — and break line of sight before the search cools down. Repeatable: if the cops catch you or the level drops too early, just build it up and try again.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back-to-back without losing your wanted level — the trick is keeping the heat the whole time, so do not let the cops lose you between robberies. Pick three shops close together, plan the route in advance, and keep moving: rob, leave fast, hit the next one before the wanted level fades. If the level drops, the chain breaks and you start the count again.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles across Leonida. A WAiNK scan is enough to count a vehicle (GameMapa), so scan every new vehicle you see rather than only the ones you drive. Vehicles are everywhere — traffic, parked cars, boats and aircraft all count toward discovery — so this builds passively if you scan as you travel, and it pairs with the WAiNK and exploration trophies.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — the slow-motion aiming mode. Set it up where enemies cluster: start a fight with a group close together, trigger Combat Focus, and chain headshots while time is slowed. If you run out of targets before five, pick a busier fight and try again; attempts are free.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the Vice City International Airport. In plain terms: leave the airport in an aircraft that was not scheduled to take you, i.e. steal a plane and take off. The airport is a restricted area, so expect a wanted level; get to a plane quickly, take off, and the trophy pops once you are airborne and away.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The Rhino is the military tank, and this trophy is about dealing with them — the description is deliberately cryptic, as PlayStation's hidden trophies often are. Expect it to involve Rhinos showing up at high wanted levels: reach the wanted level where the military responds, then survive or destroy the tanks. Check the guide sources if the exact trigger is still unclear when you reach it; this entry will be updated as the community pins it down.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth robbery, not a smash-and-grab. Plan the approach: go in quiet, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails the condition; leave, let the heat die down, and try again with a slower approach.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — the silver for the big robberies. Bank vaults are the high-end heist targets: each one needs planning and a clean getaway, and the escape is part of the requirement, so getting the money is not enough — you must get away clean. Do all five across the run; they are repeatable targets, so a failed escape just means another attempt.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run routes around Leonida; intercept one, stop it, take the cash, and then escape the wanted level that follows. The escape is part of the trophy, so have a getaway vehicle ready before you hit the truck — a fast car parked nearby beats stealing one under fire.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida (GameMapa). This is the map-completion trophy: visit every named area on the map. It pairs with almost everything else — the stranger strands, the WAiNK scans, the meditation spots — since covering the map is how you find them. Use the in-game map to spot areas you have never entered, and sweep the corners (the islands and the far north) that the story never takes you to.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs (GameMapa). Each gang runs its own operations around Leonida; hit one operation per gang and the trophy pops. Keep track of which gangs you have hit — the tracker here is made for exactly that — and work through the map gang by gang.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — one of the game's quiet, scenic moments. Head to a bar or venue on Ocean Beach with a view of the water, order a cocktail, and enjoy it. This is a hidden trophy with a deliberately vague description (GameMapa lists it among the five hidden trophies that were still unsolved at launch), so if it does not pop at the first beach bar, try the venues along the Ocean Beach front until it does.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — a nod to the series' famous showroom escape. Find a vehicle showroom, get in a car inside it, and drive straight out through the glass. This is another of the hidden trophies GameMapa listed as unsolved at launch, so if the first showroom does not trigger it, try other showrooms around Vice City until the smash registers.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — bowl a game there. GTA Scoop's guide notes this one involves stealing all 3 key valuables at Kingpin Bowling, so treat the alley as more than a game of bowling: play through and take the valuables it holds. Bowling itself is one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so you will be at an alley anyway.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. GTA Scoop's guide ties this one to maxing out strength with both Jason and Lucia — the partnership, built up together. Train both characters' strength (gyms and physical activity) until both are maxed, and the trophy should pop. The description is deliberately vague, as hidden trophies are; if it does not pop at max strength, check the community guides linked in the sources.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse. GameMapa ties this trophy to the Criminal Profile: perform 500 actions that affect your Criminal Profile and it pops. That means playing the game your way — the crimes, choices and consequences accumulate across the whole run — so it builds passively. It is not missable; it is a long count that rewards simply playing through the story and the side content.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. The description is a riddle, as hidden trophies are — GameMapa listed this among the five hidden trophies still unsolved at launch. The plain reading is that something in the game needs a second attempt: fail an activity or a challenge once, then succeed on the retry. If it does not pop from ordinary retries, check the community guides in the sources for the exact trigger once it is pinned down.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? Another riddle trophy — GameMapa listed it among the five hidden trophies still unsolved at launch. The description points at a strange, one-off event in the world: witness something unusual (an easter egg, a random encounter, a weird moment in Leonida) and the trophy pops. Explore the map's odd corners and pay attention to random events; the community guides in the sources are the place to check for the exact event once it is found.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, hit someone with a melee weapon. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing the melee weapon from the car window, and connect. It is a stunt-style trophy — a bit of aim, a bit of timing — and it is repeatable, so keep trying until the hit lands. Pick a quiet street so you are not fighting traffic while you line it up.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists; they cannot be spent directly, so move them through your contacts to clean them. Keep robbing (bank vaults, armored trucks, shops) and keep laundering the proceeds — the $250,000 is cumulative, so it builds across the whole run and pairs with the crime trophies in stage 5 of the roadmap.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative, in any shops, on anything. This builds passively as you buy weapons, ammo, clothes, food and vehicles through the run. If you reach the endgame short of the total, the fastest top-up is buying expensive items you actually want (weapons and vehicle upgrades beat consumables). It pairs with Treat Yo Self's natural spending and with the laundering economy of Dime on the Dollar.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties (GameMapa). Garages are the property purchases that store your vehicle collection — buy each one as it becomes available and the trophy pops when the eighth is yours. They cost money, so this fits late in the run once the laundering and robbery income is flowing, and it pairs with Whip It Good, since a garage full of discovered vehicles is the point of both.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Scooter Bros app is the in-game vehicle service: register vehicles you own or find through it, and count to ten. Any ten vehicles will do, so register the ones you already drive rather than hunting rare ones — and combine it with Whip It Good, since discovering vehicles and registering them go together.
trophies.name: On the Spot
